entries.title: The command bar offers Quick search
entries.body: On an article of your own, asking the command bar to find something offers Quick search first and an exact-word Find second; choosing Quick search opens Search with your words in it. In a narrow window or on a touch screen, the bottom bar no longer shows a lone lightning button there. The / key still works.

entries.title: Chat's list shows more of each conversation
entries.body: In Chat's list of conversations, a title that was cut short is filled out from your first question, up to a limit. In a narrow window, a title can run to three lines and the preview of the last message to two, so it is easier to tell the conversations apart on a phone.

entries.title: Search gains a clear button and truer timing
entries.body: When the Search box has words in it, a cross appears that clears them, as the Escape key does; a screen without a keyboard had no way to do that. The thorough search, which looks for meaning, says it takes usually about ten seconds; the old wording overstated the wait.

entries.title: The library shifts less as it loads
entries.body: Each article in your library keeps a line free for its topics while they are on their way, which reduces how much the page moves when they arrive. Topics that wrap onto more lines can still make a row taller. On a phone, a wrapped line of an article's details no longer starts with a stray dot.

entries.title: An answer stays put while it is written
entries.body: While a typed answer was being written, the conversation kept scrolling to the bottom, so its first sentence could leave the screen while you were reading it. Your question now sits near the top, or the start of the answer does if the question is long. The Latest button jumps to the end once and then stops following.

entries.title: Dates without a year get a margin note
entries.body: Timeline events whose date has no year were shown in the Timeline panel but had no note in the margin. They now get one, using the article's own wording for the date, beside a quoted passage that contains it. Where no quoted passage contains that wording, there is no note.

entries.title: Unexpected data no longer takes a panel down
entries.body: A copy of the app left open across several updates, as one opened from a home-screen icon can be, could be sent a label it did not know, and a panel or a passage's notes would vanish. It now falls back to a general wording. Separately, an article stored with part of its outline missing no longer fails to open.

entries.title: Maths can recover after an update
entries.body: In a copy of the app left open across an update, the part that draws maths could fail to load, leaving formulas as raw TeX, the code they are written in. The app now checks whether it is out of date and can reload itself once for each different version it finds live. If that does not help, the formulas stay as written.
